questions.question: Basic use cases Xu lists for a URL shortener include:
options: Only deleting URLs with no create or redirect paths.
Shorten long→short, redirect short→long, plus HA/scalability/fault tolerance.
Training ML models on video frames exclusively.
Replacing DNS for the entire public internet.
questions.explanation: URL shortening… URL redirecting… High availability, scalability, and fault tolerance

reference.book: System Design Interview - An Insider's Guide by Alex Xu

questions.question: A 301 redirect implies the short URL mapping is treated as:
options: Temporary, so every later click still hits the shortener first.
Permanent, so browsers may cache and skip the shortener later.
Invalid, so clients must poll with HTTP 100 Continue.
Encrypted, so only POST can resolve the alias.
questions.explanation: A 301 redirect shows that the requested URL is “permanently” moved

reference.book: System Design Interview - An Insider's Guide by Alex Xu
reference.excerpt: Candidate: Can you give an example of how a URL shortener work?

questions.question: A reason to prefer 302 over 301 for a shortener is:
options: 302 always reduces shortener load more than 301.
302 keeps traffic flowing through the shortener for easier click analytics.
302 disables HTTPS for all subsequent navigations.
302 stores the long URL only in the DNS CNAME record.
questions.explanation: if analytics is important, 302 redirect is a better choice

reference.book: System Design Interview - An Insider's Guide by Alex Xu
reference.excerpt: Integrating an analytics solution to the URL shortener could help to answer important questions like how many people click on a link?

books.book: Fundamentals of Software Architecture, 2nd Edition by Mark Richards and Neal Ford
books.excerpt: This sort of complexity is called accidental complexity: in short, “we have made a problem hard.” Architects sometimes add complexity to prove their worth when things seem too simple, or to guarantee that they are always kept in the loop on decisions or even to maintain job security.

books.book: Designing Data-Intensive Applications by Martin Kleppmann
books.excerpt: Compared to data flowing through databases (as described in “Dataflow Through Databases”), we can make a simplifying assumption in the case of dataflow through services: it is reasonable to assume that all the servers will be updated first and all the clients second.

questions.question: Xu’s example shortened URL charset is described as:
options: Only punctuation and whitespace characters.
Digits 0-9 and letters a-z / A-Z (base62-style).
Only hexadecimal with mandatory dashes every two chars.
Only Unicode combining marks, with no ASCII letters.
questions.explanation: combination of numbers (0-9) and characters (a-z, A-Z)

reference.book: System Design Interview - An Insider's Guide by Alex Xu
reference.excerpt: Interviewer: Shortened URL can be a combination of numbers (0-9) and characters (a-z, A-Z).

questions.question: With 100M new URLs/day, write QPS is roughly:
options: 100 million writes per second sustained all day.
About 100M/86400 ≈ ~1k+ writes/sec order of magnitude (Xu ~1160).
Exactly 2 writes per second regardless of assumptions.
Zero writes because shorteners only redirect.
